catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 1 results in healthy volunteers
detailed_catalyst_text: Results from a Phase 1 study in healthy Japanese adults were presented at a major dermatology meeting. The study showed rapid, sustained STAT6 degradation with dose-proportional PK and a favorable safety profile. These findings were consistent with prior studies and support broader clinical development in Type 2 inflammation.
catalyst_text_evidence: Kymera Therapeutics, Inc. ... announced that the results from the Phase 1 study of KT-621, its first-in-class, oral STAT6 degrader, in healthy Japanese adults were shared in an oral presentation at the Japanese Dermatological Association (JDA) Annual Meeting being held 2026-06-11 to 2026-06-14, in Kyoto, Japan. KT-621 demonstrated a favorable PK profile, including rapid absorption and dose-proportional increases in plasma exposure, and rapid, sustained STAT6 degradation in blood, with median degradation ≥98% at both dose levels at Day 7. KT-621 was well tolerated with a favorable safety profile across both doses.

catalyst_text: Initiated first in human Phase 1 trial
detailed_catalyst_text: The first participant was dosed in a first-in-human Phase 1 study of an oral IRAK4 degrader in healthy volunteers and patients with hidradenitis suppurativa. This confirms trial initiation in HS and begins clinical safety and pharmacokinetic evaluations, and it also triggered a collaboration milestone payment.
catalyst_text_evidence: Kymera Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:KYMR) ... today announced that the first participant has been dosed in the first-in-human Phase 1 clinical trial evaluating KT-485 (SAR447971), an oral, potent and selective IRAK4 degrader, in adult healthy volunteers and hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) patients. Under the terms of the collaboration, dosing of the first participant triggered a $20 million milestone payment to Kymera from Sanofi.

catalyst_text: Received FDA Fast Track for eosinophilic asthma
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA granted Fast Track designation to KT-621 for moderate to severe eosinophilic asthma. This regulatory milestone can facilitate more frequent FDA interactions and potentially expedite development and review. The program is currently being evaluated in a global Phase 2b asthma study.
catalyst_text_evidence: Kymera Therapeutics, Inc. ... announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted Fast Track designation to KT-621, its first-in-class oral STAT6 degrader, for the treatment of moderate to severe eosinophilic asthma. KT-621 is currently being studied in two global Phase 2b studies, including for the treatment of moderate to severe eosinophilic asthma.

catalyst_text: Previously granted FDA Fast Track for atopic dermatitis
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA had previously granted Fast Track designation to KT-621 for moderate to severe atopic dermatitis. This supports the program’s potential to address an unmet need and may expedite regulatory interactions. The compound is being studied in a Phase 2b AD trial.
catalyst_text_evidence: Fast Track designation previously granted for KT-621 for moderate to severe AD. Additionally, the KT-621 BROADEN2 Phase 2b trial in moderate to severe atopic dermatitis is ongoing, with data expected to be reported by mid-2027.

catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 1b results at dermatology meeting
detailed_catalyst_text: A late-breaking oral presentation at the American Academy of Dermatology 2026 meeting featured Phase 1b data for KT-621 in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, showing deep STAT6 degradation, biomarker reductions, and encouraging clinical activity after 28 days. The results support a compelling once-daily oral profile and inform advancement into later-stage studies for Type 2 inflammatory conditions.
catalyst_text_evidence: Kymera Therapeutics, Inc. ... today announced that the positive results from the BroADen Phase 1b atopic dermatitis (AD) clinical trial of KT-621, its first-in-class, oral STAT6 degrader, were featured in a late-breaking oral presentation at the American Academy of Dermatology (AAD) Annual Meeting. Data shared at AAD from the BroADen Phase 1b single-arm, open-label trial showed consistent impact across multiple pharmacodynamic and clinical measures evaluated in 22 patients with moderate-to-severe AD. After 28 days of once-daily oral dosing, KT-621 demonstrated deep STAT6 degradation across both the 100 and 200 mg dose groups tested, with median reductions of 94% in skin and 98% in blood. These biological effects translated into encouraging clinical activity with similar results across both dose groups. KT-621 was well tolerated with a favorable safety profile.

catalyst_text: Initiated Phase 2b dosing in eosinophilic asthma study
detailed_catalyst_text: Initiation of dosing in the Phase 2b BREADTH trial in adults with moderate to severe eosinophilic asthma was announced. The global randomized, placebo-controlled study evaluates three doses over 12 weeks with change in FEV1 as the primary endpoint. This milestone advances the program into mid-stage development in asthma.
catalyst_text_evidence: Kymera Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:KYMR), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company advancing a new class of oral small molecule degrader medicines for immunological diseases, today announced that it recently initiated dosing in its BREADTH Phase 2b clinical trial evaluating KT-621, an oral, highly selective, potent degrader of STAT6, in patients with moderate to severe eosinophilic asthma. The KT-621 BREADTH Phase 2b clinical trial is a global, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging study evaluating the efficacy, safety and tolerability of three doses of KT-621 in approximately 264 adult patients with moderate to severe eosinophilic asthma over 12 weeks.

catalyst_text: Received Fast Track and positive Phase 1b data
detailed_catalyst_text: FDA granted Fast Track designation for the treatment of moderate to severe atopic dermatitis, enabling enhanced regulatory interactions and potential expedited pathways. The company also recently reported positive results from the BroADen Phase 1b trial in atopic dermatitis, showing pharmacodynamic activity, biomarker modulation, clinical improvements, and favorable safety. These milestones support continued advancement of an oral STAT6 degrader for Type 2 inflammatory disease.
catalyst_text_evidence: Kymera Therapeutics, Inc. ... today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted Fast Track designation to KT-621, its first-in-class, oral STAT6 degrader, for the treatment of moderate to severe atopic dermatitis (AD). The Company recently reported positive results from the BroADen Phase 1b AD trial, in which KT-621 demonstrated the potential to provide a once-daily oral treatment for Type 2 inflammatory diseases across every measure evaluated, including STAT6 degradation, biomarker modulation, clinical activity, impact on comorbid Type 2 diseases, and safety.

catalyst_text: Positive Phase 1b results and Phase 2b initiated
detailed_catalyst_text: Reported positive results from the BroADen Phase 1b atopic dermatitis study, showing strong biomarker modulation, deep STAT6 degradation, and meaningful improvements in clinical endpoints with a favorable safety profile. Additionally, the BROADEN2 Phase 2b trial in atopic dermatitis is underway with patient dosing commenced, advancing the program to mid-stage development.
catalyst_text_evidence: Kymera Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:KYMR), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company advancing a new class of oral small molecule degrader medicines for immunological diseases, today announced positive clinical results from the BroADen Phase 1b atopic dermatitis (AD) clinical trial of KT-621, its first-in-class, oral STAT6 degrader medicine. The Company's KT-621 BROADEN2 Phase 2b trial in moderate to severe AD patients is ongoing, and patient dosing has commenced.

catalyst_text: Initiated Phase 2b trial completed Phase 1b dosing
detailed_catalyst_text: Initiated dosing in a Phase 2b randomized, placebo-controlled study in moderate to severe atopic dermatitis. The program had previously completed dosing in a Phase 1b AD trial, supporting advancement into mid-stage development.
catalyst_text_evidence: Kymera Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:KYMR), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company advancing a new class of oral small molecule degrader medicines for immunological diseases, today announced that it recently initiated dosing in its BROADEN2 Phase 2b clinical trial evaluating KT-621, an oral, highly selective, potent degrader of STAT6, in patients with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis (AD). Additionally, the Company previously announced it completed dosing in the KT-621 BroAdEn Phase 1b trial in AD, with data to be reported in December 2025.
